summary: “Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy, priced into the national score). No country-unique finding beyond insurance-coverage details a visitor never encounters. Clearly above the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: July 2026 anti-trans legal-risk assessment map (Erin In The Morning, republication): scores every US state for transgender adults and lists Vermont among the fifteen 'Most Protective' states (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA) - states with refuge protections for people fleeing restrictive states and legal reinforcement of care access, 'the most likely to counteract federal anti-trans regulations'. The same update moved Idaho from 'Worst Laws' to 'Do Not Travel' (felony bathroom ban, up to 5 years, partially blocked but in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists) and rated the country overall 'Worst Policies In Effect'.

Movement Advancement Project equality map (data as of 25 Sep 2026): 16 states plus DC have 'shield' laws protecting access to transgender health care - shielding recipients and providers from civil or criminal actions by states where care is banned; 38% of the transgender population (13+) lives under a shield law, 56% under none. Vermont is among the shield-law states cited in the dossier's 'Most Protective' line for this unit.

localsOnly: Vermont's only recorded differences from its protective peers are insurance-coverage details a visitor never encounters.
